clue.text: In Hull, they put a stop to leaks and lies

definitions.text: In Hull, they put a stop to leaks
definitions.meaning: workers who pack the seams of a ship's hull with oakum and pitch to keep the water out
an old slang word for big lies or whoppers, as in Chambers

explanation.walkthrough: Hull looks like the English city, but it is a ship's hull. The second sense is an old slang word for a whopping lie.
explanation.definitionFit: Seam-sealing shipwrights stop leaks, and the same word is old slang for outrageous untruths.

clue.text: Draw together impedimenta without point

indicators.note: used in its old sense of outside, so the gear word wraps round the point

parts.note: impedimenta is baggage or equipment, a kit
N, north, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone gathers up their baggage, with nothing sharp in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' here means outside: KIT goes round N.
explanation.definitionFit: To knit is to draw parts together, as brows are knitted in a frown or bones knit after a break.

clue.text: Rhyme scheme found in poetry from Crete and Troy

indicators.note: the letters are made from the island's name, worked into a new order

parts.note: t is the abbreviation for troy weight

explanation.surface: A verse form turns up in ancient poems of Crete and Troy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' tells you the letters of CRETE are rearranged, giving TERCE; Troy is not the city but troy weight, abbreviated T.
explanation.definitionFit: A three-line stanza, usually rhymed together or interlinked, is a set verse form found in poems.

clue.text: Hammer the guy around fifty and scoff

indicators.note: the word for a man is placed round the Roman numeral for fifty

parts.note: a guy is a man, a male
L is the Roman numeral for fifty
to scoff is to eat greedily; ate is its past form

explanation.surface: Someone attacks a man, then eats heartily.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scoff' must be read as past tense, scoffed, for its piece to fit; 'Hammer' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To malleate is to beat metal thin with blows, the literal sense of hammering.

clue.text: He'll sip drinks, teas maybe in cold weather

indicators.note: the shuffled letters are placed inside the season word

parts.note: winter is the season of cold weather

indicators.note: maybe suggests the letters could be in some other arrangement

explanation.surface: Someone sips hot drinks such as tea through the cold months.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' turns TEAS into ETAS, which goes 'in' WINTER.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional taster sips wines to judge their quality, so he is a man who samples drinks.

clue.text: Grass making charge about skinhead and copper

indicators.note: the payment word goes round the other two pieces

parts.note: a charge is a fee
the head, or first letter, of skin is S
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper

explanation.surface: A fee is charged against a shaven-headed thug and a policeman.
explanation.walkthrough: Skinhead and copper suggest a thug and a policeman, but skinhead is just the first letter of skin, and copper the chemical element.
explanation.definitionFit: Fescue is a genus of tufted grasses common in lawns and pasture.

clue.text: Exercising spaniels is pleasant enough

indicators.note: exercising dogs moves them about, so the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Walking the spaniels is quite a nice chore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Exercising' rearranges SPANIELS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without discomfort or trouble is agreeable enough, the loose everyday sense.

clue.text: The transmitter needs to be put right — right!

indicators.note: putting something right means sorting it out, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A radio transmitter needs fixing, and the speaker agrees emphatically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be put right' rearranges NEEDS into SENDE, then the exclaimed second 'right' adds R.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that sends out a signal is a transmitter.

clue.text: A team's remarks not generally overheard

parts.note: a team is a side, and the possessive gives side's

explanation.surface: A team's private comments are not picked up by others.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in team's is ignored, so SIDE'S gives SIDES.
explanation.definitionFit: Stage whispers meant for the audience and not for the other actors are remarks others are not supposed to catch.

clue.text: Far too much money is put into draw

indicators.note: the money letter goes inside the word for drawing a bird

parts.note: to draw a fowl is to gut it, removing its innards
L stands for pound, the British money unit, from Latin libra

explanation.surface: Excessive cash is placed in a lottery or prize draw.
explanation.walkthrough: 'draw' looks like a lottery, but to draw a fowl is to gut it.
explanation.definitionFit: A glut is an oversupply, more than can be used.

clue.text: The intermingling of flowers

parts.note: flowers read as things that flow, rivers, so this is where two streams merge, not a mixed bouquet

explanation.walkthrough: Flowers looks like blooms; read it as flow-ers, rivers.
explanation.definitionFit: The meeting point where two rivers join and their waters mix.

clue.text: It usually pours in the late afternoon

definitions.text: It usually pours in the late afternoon

parts.words: It usually pours in the late afternoon
parts.note: reads like rain arriving later in the day, but the pouring is done at British afternoon tea

explanation.walkthrough: Pours suggests rain; British afternoon tea is served around four o'clock.
explanation.definitionFit: The vessel used to serve the brew at teatime pours it out.

clue.text: Nimble guide going first, holding a small flame

indicators.note: the guide word is placed before the nimble word in the answer

parts.note: a pilot guides ships into harbour
light means nimble, as in light on one's feet

explanation.surface: An agile leader goes ahead carrying a small torch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nimble' comes first in the clue, but 'going first' sends the guide ahead of it; 'holding' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The tiny burner kept alight in a boiler or gas cooker to ignite the main jets.

clue.text: Springs for men with a seat to renovate

indicators.note: renovating something remakes it, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Seat springs for men are to be refurbished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to renovate' rearranges MEN and A SEAT; Springs looks like the coils in a seat, but is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To spring from a source is to issue or flow from it.

clue.text: Liquid, we hear, will cost money when it runs out

definitions.text: Liquid, we hear, will cost money when it runs out

parts.words: Liquid, we hear, will cost money when it runs out
parts.note: the noise made by a liquid hitting something, which also means spending freely when followed by out

explanation.walkthrough: To splash out is British idiom for spending lavishly; the word is also the noise liquid makes.
explanation.definitionFit: The noise of water striking is this word, and adding out gives a phrase for lavish spending.

clue.text: Cut up about theologian being housed in a shack

indicators.note: the two pieces are lodged inside the hut word

parts.note: a shed is a shack
re means about, concerning
DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a theologian

explanation.surface: Someone is upset that a religious scholar lives in a hut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' is not a container signal here but a piece, the short word for concerning; 'being housed in' does the containing.
explanation.definitionFit: Shredded means torn or cut into strips.

clue.text: Oriental holy man getting into bed, beaten

indicators.note: the pieces are put inside the sleeping word

parts.note: E is east, oriental meaning eastern
St is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: An Eastern guru climbs into bed after a defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: Oriental and holy man suggest an Eastern guru, but they are just the compass point and the abbreviation for saint.
explanation.definitionFit: Bested means outdone or defeated.

clue.text: Steps outside first, showing reserve

indicators.note: the steps word sits outside the abbreviation for first

parts.note: a dance is a sequence of steps
1st, written IST, is first

explanation.surface: Moving out in front shows restraint.
explanation.walkthrough: The digit 1 in the usual abbreviation for first is read as the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: Keeping one's distance means aloofness, which is reserve in manner.

clue.text: Not a particular individual

parts.note: a person who could be ... at all, not a specified someone

explanation.definitionFit: The pronoun names some person or other without specifying who.

clue.text: It could make things smoother for the home club

parts.note: a flat is a home
an iron is a golf club

explanation.surface: Something improves conditions for the local sports club.
explanation.walkthrough: The home club suggests a team playing at home; split it into two pieces, a dwelling and a golf club.
explanation.definitionFit: An old heated iron for pressing clothes smooths out creases.

clue.text: Persuade to take ale and nod off

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters are scrambled

explanation.surface: Coax someone to drink beer and fall asleep.
explanation.walkthrough: 'off' rearranges ALE and NOD.
explanation.definitionFit: To lead someone on is to entice or encourage them, often deceptively.

clue.text: Read through, then practise

parts.note: per means through or by
to use a skill is to practise it

explanation.surface: Study the material, then rehearse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Read through' looks like one phrase, but the definition is just 'Read'; 'through' gives PER.
explanation.definitionFit: To peruse is to examine a text carefully.

clue.text: Somewhat eye-catching

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both fairly, as an adverb, and attractive, as an adjective.

clue.text: Madam possibly given more lip and harassed

indicators.note: harassed suggests being bothered and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A lady of the house got cheek and was pestered.
explanation.walkthrough: Madam looks like a woman, but it is an example of a word reading the same backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Madam spells the same in both directions, an example of the type.

clue.text: Try to win over the company with a kiss

parts.note: X is a kiss, as at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Someone woos the firm with a kiss.
explanation.definitionFit: To coax is to persuade gently.

clue.text: Company, almost all of whose product is fuel

indicators.note: almost means not quite all of the word, so its last letter goes

explanation.surface: A firm whose output is almost entirely fuel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' drops the last L of 'all' to give AL.
explanation.definitionFit: Coal is a fossil fuel burned for heat.

clue.text: Run after so quiet a girl

indicators.note: the run word is placed after the other two pieces

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical sign for quiet
hie is an old word for hurry or run

explanation.surface: Chase after such a shy girl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run' comes first in the clue, but 'after' places it at the end; hie is an archaic verb most solvers meet only in crosswords.
explanation.definitionFit: Sophie is a girl's given name.

clue.text: Indoor delight

definitions.meaning: read as in-door, the door one goes in by
a verb meaning charm or enrapture

explanation.definitionFit: A way in is literally an in-door, and to enchant someone is to delight them, stressed on the second syllable.
